verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) Nothing is missing. The heading is present at line 13790 with its clause number and title verbatim as printed ('12.3.6.4 General rules'), preceded by the correct anchor '' at 13789. The kind label 'missing-heading' misdescribes the file: the sole difference is the markdown '#' count. I also compared the whole page-316 body against the 300dpi render - syntax rule 4), general rules 1)-5), and sub-items a)-i) of GR 5 are all present and textually faithful. No normative text is lost. (2) The claim's premise about the PDF is vacuous. I rendered page 315 (spec_p315.png): '12.3.6 OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph', '12.3.6.1 General', '12.3.6.2 General format' and '12.3.6.3 Syntax rules' are printed in the SAME bold face, at the SAME point size, at the SAME left margin - and page 316 prints '12.3.6.4 General rules' identically. The PDF gives the PARENT clause 12.3.6 the same typographic rank as its children, so ISO's typography encodes no heading depth at all; depth lives only in the dotted clause number, which the markdown reproduces exactly. There is therefore no PDF property that '## ' contradicts. (3) The '## vs ###' split is pervasive transcription noise, not a page-316 fact. Across specs/ISO_COBOL.md, four-level clause numbers appear as '##' 162 times, '###' 620 times and '####' 24 times; three-level numbers appear as '##' 276 times, '###' 508 times and '####' 17 times. The same clause depth carries three different heading levels throughout the document, so markdown heading depth is not a structural encoding anywhere in this file. 74 of the 162 four-level '##' cases sit within 12 lines after a '## Page N' marker, identifying page-chunked transcription as a main cause - i.e. page-break furniture, an explicit rejection criterion. (4) The stated harm is neither caused nor cured by this line. The file uses '## Page 316' for page markers and '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' for the running header, and that h1 running header sits at line 13785 - between '## 12.3.6' on page 315 and the heading at 13790. Any heading-nesting walker therefore re-parents everything after 13785 under the page-316 running-header h1; promoting 12.3.6.4 to '###' would nest it under that h1, still not under 12.3.6. Heading nesting is already unusable as an outline in this transcription for reasons wholly independent of this heading, and the correct resolution key - the clause number 12.3.6.4 and the section-12-3-6-4 anchor - is present and correct. Formatting-only, meaning-preserving, systemic: not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading '12.3.6.4 General rules' is present, verbatim, with a correct '' anchor, and the entire page-316 body matches the render. The only difference is the markdown heading level ('##' rather than the siblings' '###'), which is transcription formatting metadata with no counterpart in the PDF - ISO prints 12.3.6, 12.3.6.1, 12.3.6.2, 12.3.6.3 and 12.3.6.4 in identical bold at identical size, encoding depth solely in the clause number. If anyone wants markdown heading levels normalized, that is a document-wide markdown-hygiene cleanup (162 four-level clause numbers are '##', 620 '###', 24 '####'; 276/508/17 for three-level), not a page-316 reconciliation finding, and it would not by itself make heading nesting resolvable because the per-page '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running-header h1 breaks parent-child nesting at every page boundary regardless.
